(per-note checklist) and
(specific tasks).

items: Metadata complete: title, version, created, updated, tags — all five present; tags meaningful; updated reflects the last real content change.
Parent link present if it is a child note — a para near the top reading "Parent: [[parentkey]]".
All linked keys valid — cross-check every href against the current key listing; fix or remove dead links.
Note type standard met (see below).
No stale facts: version numbers, machine/service names, config paths, bug workarounds.
JSONHTL format correct: multi-line code uses codeblock not inline code in a para; lists use {"list": {"items": [...]}} not bare arrays (bare arrays store but 500 the renderer).
Step sequences use ordered lists, not bullet lists.
Procedural notes: gotchas extracted into a named list near the end.
Mark done in notes-review with [x] DATE.

Procedural (how to do X, how to rebuild Y): ordered steps; gotchas list; cold-read test — an agent reading cold should succeed without needing context the author already had. Correct facts are paramount; verify against current reality when recently changed.
Reference (schemas, instruction sets, API docs): completeness; structure optimised for lookup not narrative; version numbers and dates noted explicitly.
Design/decision: preserve reasoning in full — "why not X" is as important as "we chose Y". Do not summarise away nuance. These notes are only useful if the reasoning survives.
Memory/context (memory/*, MEMORY/*): highest staleness priority — shape every future agent session; errors here cause repeated mistakes. Review first in any pass.
Todo/tracker: clear current-state summary at the top; completed items removed or struck; linked from TODO master index.

para: Notes with these characteristics warrant careful verification before being trusted.

items: updated more than 6 months ago and covers active infrastructure.
Specific version numbers (port versions, Python versions, package names) — versions move.
"TODO / still to verify" sections written speculatively that may have since been resolved but never marked.
Machine or service names that may no longer exist.
"Workaround for bug X" — the upstream bug may have been fixed.
Notes for projects since completed, abandoned, or substantially redesigned.

Split/merge: highest-risk operation — splitting breaks all incoming links to the original key; merging destroys a key permanently. Only where the case is overwhelming. Do last in any pass, never first.
Deletion: confirm with John before deleting anything potentially referenced. Prefer adding "archived YYYY-MM-DD, superseded by [[key]]" at the top to outright removal.
Renaming a key: never rename without updating every inbound link (CONTENTS, TRIGGERS, parent links, all referencing notes) and confirming no external system uses the old key.

heading.text: Suggested working order for a pass

items: CONTENTS + TRIGGERS — navigation skeleton; everything else depends on it.
memory/* and MEMORY/* — agent behaviour notes; staleness here costs every session.
Active operational clusters (radagast, uucp, hosts) — high value, recently changed.
README/* — conventions; understand before applying elsewhere.
Active project notes (hibernate-on-approach, delayrepay, popit3, envoy living docs).
PROGRAMMING_RULES/*.
Lower-priority clusters (pwsafe, ask, gloss, Z80, ideas).
Archive pass last — once living docs are solid, easier to see what the historical records are archiving against.
